facts.text: The Royal Mansour Marrakech is just a few steps from Jemaa El Fna square.
facts.excerpt: Just a few steps away from Jemaa El Fna square, beats the heart of the Marrakech palace

facts.text: The hotel is designed as a medina within a medina, with riads in place of rooms and suites and winding alleyways in place of corridors.
facts.excerpt: The rooms and suites have been replaced by luxurious riads and the corridors by winding alleyways.

facts.text: The estate covers 5 hectares, protected by the walls of the imperial city and overlooked by the Atlas Mountains.
facts.excerpt: Protected by the walls of the imperial city and overlooked by the majestic peaks of the Atlas Mountains, the emblematic Marrakech palace is at hand to guide you through its exclusive 5-hectare estate.

facts.text: Accommodation is in 53 independent riads, each unique and decorated in its own style.
facts.excerpt: The Royal Mansour Marrakech unveils a collection of 53 independent riads. In a true display of Moroccan handicraft, each riad is unique and decorated in its own deliciously enchanting style.

facts.text: The private riads have one to four bedrooms and a pool.
facts.excerpt: 53 private riads with one to four bedrooms and a pool

facts.text: Riads have lounges, shaded patios and terraces with a view of the Atlas mountains.
facts.excerpt: Cosy lounges, shaded patios, exquisite bathrooms and terraces with a view of the majestic Atlas mountains

facts.text: The Grand riad has its own garden, private swimming pool, hammam and four bedrooms.
facts.excerpt: With its garden, private swimming pool, hammam and four bedrooms, this exceptional and exclusive residence inspires the wildest dreams.

facts.text: The hotel has four signature restaurants.
facts.excerpt: Four signature restaurants in the heart of the Palace

facts.text: Le Jardin, with its swimming pool, was designed by Spanish landscape architect Luis Vallejo.
facts.excerpt: Le Jardin Royal Mansour, designed by the Spanish landscape architect Luis Vallejo, is an ode to the gardens and greenery iconic to the Ochre City.

facts.text: The spa covers 2,500 square metres.
facts.excerpt: Its medina, restaurants, gardens, 2,500 sqm spa, 53 charming riads and outstanding concierge service

facts.text: The spa has a hammam, a hairdressing salon, a gym, a heated swimming pool and an atrium.
facts.excerpt: Feel the soothing effects of our hammam, outstanding treatments, hairdressing salon, gym, heated swimming pool, magnificent atrium

facts.text: The kids' club is in Le Jardin de Lila.
facts.excerpt: In Le Jardin de Lila, the Royal Mansour rolls out the red carpet for children

facts.text: The hotel offers cooking, patisserie and mixology workshops.
facts.excerpt: SIGNATURE WORKSHOP Cooking workshops

facts.text: The concierge plans individually tailored programmes for exploring Marrakech and Morocco.
facts.excerpt: they will plan out an individually tailored programme for each of your adventures into the Moroccan Kingdom

facts.text: At the 50 Best Hotels 2026, Royal Mansour Marrakech was ranked 26th and named Best Hotel in Africa.
facts.excerpt: Ranked 26th among the world's finest hotels and named Best Hotel in Africa

facts.text: The hotel is owned by the King of Morocco.
facts.excerpt: the hotel is owned by none other than the King of Morocco himself

facts.text: After a private entry courtyard with a fountain, each riad is a three-story accommodation.
facts.excerpt: After passing through your own private entry courtyard complete with fountain, you enter your three-story accommodation.

facts.text: All riads come with 24/7 access to a personal butler.
facts.excerpt: All riads come with 24/7 access to a personal butler

facts.text: A network of hidden tunnels and elevators lets staff serve guests discreetly.
facts.excerpt: the property's network of hidden tunnels and elevators, which allow the staff to respond to each and every request in a magically discreet fashion

facts.text: Chef Yannick Alleno oversees the property's food and beverage outposts, which include La Grande Table Marocaine.
facts.excerpt: make sure you secure a reservation at the fine dining destination La Grande Table Marocaine

facts.text: The hotel offers an exclusive excursion to the nearby home of the late perfumer Serge Lutens, which is not open to the public.
facts.excerpt: The hotel offers an exclusive excursion to the nearby home of the late master perfumer Serge Lutens, which is not open to the public and does not allow photos.

facts.text: Wi-Fi is free.
facts.excerpt:
Is there a charge for Wi-Fi?
No charge.

facts.text: The hotel is close to the Medina but its layout makes it feel like a private estate.
facts.excerpt: The location couldn't be more central, but the layout of property makes it feel like you're on a private estate miles away from the hustle and bustle.

facts.text: Built by many local master craftsmen (CNT gives both 1,200 and 1,500).
facts.excerpt: It took over 1,500 local artisans to create this

facts.text: Known to insiders as the best hotel in Marrakech.
facts.excerpt: known to insiders as the “best hotel in Marrakech”

contradictions.note: CNT summary says 1,200 master craftsmen; CNT body says over 1,500 local artisans

sources.excerpt: took 1,200 master craftsmen over three years to construct
It took over 1,500 local artisans to create this
